what_this_is: 20 technique rows from four media, with the crossing fields the 2026-10-30 backfill gave them (ids renamed, source addresses left out), the vocabulary their terms come from (every property, the mechanisms these rows hold; vectors left out: crossing reads terms), and a goal in a fifth medium.

request.goal: a sales page for a budgeting app

rows.name: Staggered text entrance from a clipped baseline
rows.description: A motion idea seen on 138 of the 200 catalogued sites, kept here by the reason it works so it can be reused in any medium.

needs.says: text split into units
a clip or mask on each unit
a delay between units

produces: a headline that arrives in reading order
large type that feels placed

rows.name: Pointer as a live input to the scene
rows.description: A motion idea seen on 75 of the 200 catalogued sites, kept here by the reason it works so it can be reused in any medium.

needs.says: a pointer position read on every update
an eased follower value

produces: a surface that leans toward or away from the hand
a feeling that the surface is physically there

rows.name: Scroll position as a playhead
rows.description: A motion idea seen on 74 of the 200 catalogued sites, kept here by the reason it works so it can be reused in any medium.

needs.says: a timeline of the sequence
a pinned region
a mapping from input distance to timeline progress

produces: a sequence the person plays at their own pace
the person runs the story forward and back

rows.name: Real objects that obey simple physics
rows.description: A motion idea seen on 45 of the 200 catalogued sites, kept here by the reason it works so it can be reused in any medium.

needs.says: a physics step
collision on each object
a pointer force

produces: a pile or model that reacts when touched
a person who stays longer to play

rows.name: Immersive Garden
rows.description: A Agency & Studio site rated 9/10 for motion, built with Three.js, Nuxt, WebGL; its motion is made of plaster relief reveal; mouse-reactive lighting; serif copy fade-up; loader-to-hero handoff; rising showreel frame.

needs.says: a loader that hands over to the first view
a fixed hero composition
light that follows the pointer

produces: a hushed, gallery-calm first view
a wait that ends in arrival

rows.name: Set the phone down to begin, so the viewer sees the shot being made
rows.description: Named only by title. Reading: the clip opens on the person placing the camera down, stepping back and starting, which shows the moment of setting up and reads as unscripted. Filmable alone with a stable surface.

needs.says: a stable surface to set the device on
a clip that starts before the first line

produces: the take reads as unscripted
the setting up is seen before the message

rows.name: Mirror format: two identical people, one small repeated change, a counter, and the viewer sees themselves
rows.description: Two figures start identical at week 1. A visible counter advances. One adds a small fixed step each week and the other does not; by week 13 the gap is large and the closing line says same effort, only one added weight. The viewer realises they are the one who did not. In the example (16 seconds, vertical) the numbers are the poster's claims: both deadlift 60 kg at week 1, one adds 5 kg a week and lifts 120 kg at week 13, 7 million views across 5 videos on an account 8 days old, 3 million on the top one, and the poster guesses an AI model made it. Works for anything that compounds: savings, writing, practice, outreach.

needs.says: two identical starting figures
one small repeated change
a visible counter

produces: the viewer sees their own inaction as the cause of a worse result
an urge to make the one change

rows.name: Every number from the tool; say no data rather than invent one
rows.description: The strategist prompt tells the agent to take every figure from the library tool's answers and to answer no data when the tool has none. In the recipe this is a rule on every step, not just a line in a prompt.

needs.says: a tool that returns the figures
a rule that applies to every step

produces: every figure traced to a tool answer
missing data stated as no data

rows.name: Every scene ends on a small open question
rows.description: Each scene closes on something unresolved (a daydream, a reveal window, a line that invites 'what next?'), so attention carries across every cut.

needs.says: an unresolved beat at the end of each scene
a next scene that answers it

produces: attention carries across every cut
viewers stay through the whole piece

rows.name: Short pieces feed long-form where revenue per viewer is higher
rows.description: Use short reels to send viewers to long relaxing YouTube videos linked from the bio, where ad money per viewer is much larger. Products and brand deals fit once an audience trusts the character.

needs.says: an audience that already trusts the character
a longer place linked from the short pieces
a reason to keep watching after the first piece

produces: more time spent per visitor
more income per visitor from longer pieces

rows.name: Bento
rows.description: Modular grid layout with card-like blocks, clear hierarchy, soft spacing, and subtle visual contrast for organized, scannable interfaces.

needs.says: items that group into equal units
a few clear levels of importance

produces: each block is scanned on its own
an organised overview at a glance

rows.name: Binance.US
rows.description: Crypto exchange. Bold yellow accent on monochrome, trading-floor urgency.

needs.says: one bright signal on calm neutrals
moments that call for a quick decision

produces: the eye jumps to the action
a sense that time is short

rows.name: Cal.com
rows.description: Open-source scheduling. Clean neutral UI, developer-oriented simplicity.

needs.says: few visual cues competing for attention
a task the person already knows

produces: the next step is obvious
starting a task takes less effort

rows.name: Claude (Anthropic)
rows.description: Anthropic's AI assistant. Warm terracotta accent, clean editorial layout.

needs.says: one warm accent in a neutral field
a clear reading order for long text

produces: a human, thoughtful feel
long text is easy to follow

rows.name: Corporate
rows.description: Professional, brand-aligned design with structured grids, minimalist layouts, and consistent enterprise patterns.

needs.says: consistent patterns across many teams
a structured grid

produces: the brand reads as dependable
a steady look across teams

rows.name: Static shot
rows.description: Camera does not move at all; the frame stays put for the whole clip.

needs.says: a subject worth holding on
a fixed framing for the full length

produces: the subject is watched without distraction
a calm, steady feel

rows.name: Slow zoom in
rows.description: Lens slowly tightens, so the subject grows in frame without the camera moving.

needs.says: a subject that holds the eye
time for the change to build

produces: attention narrows onto the subject slowly
a building sense of expectation

rows.name: Crash zoom in
rows.description: Punchy near-instant zoom snap onto the target, used for sudden emphasis.

needs.says: one target worth a sudden jump
calm moments around it

produces: attention snaps to the target
a beat of surprise

rows.name: Low tracking
rows.description: Camera moves very low, at ground or below-waist height, beside the subject's path, emphasising feet, wheels, ground.

needs.says: a moving subject with feet, wheels or ground detail
a low path beside it

produces: the ground and motion feel close and heavy
the subject feels powerful

rows.name: Crane up
rows.description: Camera rises on a boom arm, lifting and revealing the scene from higher up.

needs.says: a scene whose parts must be seen together
a clear view of the whole

produces: the viewer sees how the parts fit
the scene's scale is understood

mechanism.says: Why a technique works, in words about what it does to a person or a system, never about the medium it was found in.

terms.says: A small, equal set of named parts is grouped so a person holds the whole as one unit.
An unanswered question held in view keeps attention until it is closed.
An unexpected number makes a person stop and reread the claim.
A band over one key word sets it apart from the words around it.
A visible response to each action keeps the person acting and shows them their effect.
Typed input with measured pauses and printed output in chunks matches how real work unfolds, so the result is believed.
Items that arrive one after another in a fixed rhythm let the eye follow each in turn.
A fixed framing lets the subject hold all the attention without motion competing for it.
A limited palette reads as chosen rather than defaulted, and one accent becomes the point of focus.
A wait filled with a rising signal turns idle time into expectation of what comes next.
Pulling back after the detail shows how each part fits the whole.
A clear hand-off from the wait to the first real content makes the arrival feel completed.
A look tied to a known field makes a person feel that field's qualities.
Taking away the surroundings leaves only the part that matters, so it reads first.
Addressing the person as you puts them inside the scenario, so its stakes feel personal.
Letting a person steer the pace and order of a story makes them invested in what they find.
A common set of rules lets many diverging versions still work together.
Real originals with their true damage show that the material is genuine.
A serif heading against a plain body text separates the heading from the rest at a glance.
Repeating a known element makes continuing to follow feel like the natural next step.
A measure with no data scores low and says so, so a guess is not counted as proof.
A small, free first step builds enough trust that a larger step feels natural to take.
Warm hues on a soft neutral make a surface feel inviting and human.
A bright signal in a calm field makes a person feel time is short and act now.
Restrained, sober surfaces signal that the maker is competent and can be relied on.
A sudden jump in scale or speed forces attention onto one thing.
A view from below the subject's height makes it look larger and more dominant.

property.says: The abstract property of a person or a system that a technique changes or needs, such as attention over time, trust, perceived effort, recognisability or reproducibility.

How much work or exposure a person feels an action will cost.
How long a wait feels, separate from how long it is.
How open a person is to being asked to buy or act.

How well a choice follows from the evidence behind it.
How easily a person reads shapes or words.
How much work it takes to make each new piece.
How worth keeping or sharing a person judges a thing to be.
How clearly a person can tell who said or did something.
How much a person believes a claim or result.
How closely a result matches what the person meant.
How attention holds or fades as something unfolds.
How easily a person sees the current state of an automated process.
How far along a person feels they are toward a goal.
The judgement a person forms in the opening moments of meeting something.
How real a shown process or object feels to a person.
How easily a thing can be changed without breaking the rest.
How the sense of a picture changes when its parts are recombined.
How three-dimensional a scene feels to a person.
How widely a person believes others agree or act.
How big a person judges an object to be relative to others.
How much a person feels their own choices set the speed and order of what they see.
How lively and forceful a design feels to a person.
